question: Coal, petroleum, and kerosene are examples of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**fossil fuels**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Fossil fuel is formed by natural processes.
 
• Fossil fuels range from volatile materials with low carbon-to-hydrogen ratios (like methane) to liquids (like petroleum), to nonvolatile materials composed of almost pure carbon, like Anthracite coal.
 
• It is formed such as the anaerobic decomposition of buried dead organisms.
 
• These types of organisms and their resulting fossil fuels typically have an age of millions of years, and sometimes more than 650 million years.
 
• These types of fuels (Fossil fuels) contain high percentages of carbon and include coal, natural gas, and petroleum.
 
• Commonly used derivatives of fossil fuels include propane and kerosene.
 
• Till 2018, the world's main primary energy sources which amount to 85% share for fossil fuels in primary energy consumption in the world consists of
 
 
• Coal (27%) 
 
• Petroleum (34%), and
 
• Natural gas (24%)​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Renewable resources **are natural resources that can be replenished or regenerated, and clean energy resources are renewable resources that have a low or zero carbon footprint: 
 
• **Renewable resources**
 
 
• **These resources can be converted into clean energy:**
 
• Wind: The kinetic energy from moving air can be converted into mechanical power.
 
• Solar: Sunlight can be converted into electricity or heat.
 
• Water: Hydroelectric power is generated by forcing water through tunnels in a dam to turn turbines.
 
• Biomass: Organic matter can be burned as fuel.
 
• Geothermal: Heat energy from the earth's crust can be used for power and heating.
 
 
 
• **Clean energy resources**
 
 
• **These renewable resources have a low or zero carbon footprint:**
 
• Solar: Solar power plants use photovoltaic cells to convert sunlight directly into electricity.
 
• Wind turbines: These machines use the motion of wind to turn blades and produce power.
 
• Fuel cells: These technologies produce power and heat with low or zero emissions.
